column4: Description
Visual remains fixed while surrounding narrative content scrolls.
Scrolling progresses through a series of predefined narrative states.
Visual elements change, morph, or transform based on scroll position.
Scrolling controls the movement or viewpoint of a map, 3D scene, or camera.
Different visual layers move at different speeds to create a sense of depth.
Animation progresses, loops, or responds directly to the user's scroll position.
User adjusts a continuous variable and immediately sees its effect.
User physically moves an object from one position to another.
User directly creates, edits, draws, erases, or modifies elements on a canvas.
User directly activates, moves, connects, or changes individual nodes or elements.
User directly controls the execution or parameters of a simulated system.
User performs physical or game-like actions to influence the system or outcome.
Additional information appears when the pointer hovers over an element.
Additional information is revealed after the user clicks an element.
Small contextual information appears when interacting with a specific element.
Hovering emphasizes an element and/or its related information.
Contextual labels or explanations appear through interaction.
Hovering or selecting a geographic element reveals additional information.
User switches between two predefined states or views.
User moves a divider to compare two states, images, or datasets.
User selects one of several predefined views using a set of options.
User switches between different content or data views.
Multiple states or datasets are displayed simultaneously for comparison.
The comparison changes dynamically based on the user's selections.
An interaction with one element causes another element or view to respond.
Multiple visualizations update together to represent the same user action.
Selecting data in one view filters related data across other views.
Changes or selections in either of two connected views affect the other.
Navigation controls remain available as the user moves through the experience.
An overview provides access to different sections of the experience.
A menu allows users to move between different sections or destinations.
Tabs provide direct access to different sections or views.
User progresses through content one step at a time.
Swiping moves between screens, panels, or narrative states.
Arrows or keyboard controls allow sequential movement through content.
Users follow links to explore related content at their own pace.
User enters a query to find specific information.
User enters text that is used to modify or personalize the experience.
User selects one option from a predefined list.
User changes the order in which information is displayed.
User removes unwanted information to focus on a specific subset.
User-provided information changes the content or experience specifically for them.
User adds or removes layers to control which information is visible.
One visual form smoothly transforms into another while maintaining visual continuity.
The same object visually persists while its representation or position changes.
Animation traces movement along a geographic or spatial route.
Animation communicates movement, direction, or flow through a system.
A complex object separates or expands to reveal its internal components.
A grouped representation transitions into its individual elements.
Animation communicates a change from one state or condition to another.
User is asked to predict an outcome before seeing the actual data or result.
User makes a guess and the actual value is subsequently revealed for comparison.
User visually draws or constructs their prediction before seeing the actual result.
System provides feedback based on the user's own input, behaviour, or prediction.
User's response is compared against another benchmark, dataset, or population.
An interaction produces a reward, acknowledgement, or reinforcing response.
User can revisit or replay a previous action, process, or sequence.
User controls or triggers audio as part of the experience.
User controls or triggers video content.
A non-interactive visual provides an overall summary or orientation.
Static visual content supports the narrative or communicates contextual information.
A visual encoding decision involving shape; it does not describe a user interaction.
